structured.answer: According to the page I would open an account at Pesagot (פסגות) and buy "אי.בי.אי. מחקה ת"א 125 (4A)". With 10,000 now and 500 a month, after 10 years I'd have about 86,045 ₪ out of 70,000 put in. But a minus sign next to that fund scared me and I never got to choose any amounts, so I'd ask my son before doing anything.

stuck.why: It opens with English letters (MSCI World, S&P 500) and 'מדד', which to me is the price index on the news. I almost left. Only my task kept me reading.
10,000 and 500 were already filled in. I didn't change them and didn't touch the sliders, so the 86,045 is the site's example and not my own amounts.
'−1,030 ₪ לעומת הבחירה שלכם' has a minus. I wasn't sure whether that's a loss, so I backed away from that option.
'−0.04% בשנה · שנה אחת' under the fund it recommends. A minus on the very fund I'm meant to buy. Did it lose money? This is where I stopped trusting it.
Not sure whether 86,045 is what I'll really get or something adjusted for inflation

findings.what: A minus sign (−0.04%) right under the fund the page recommends, with no plain explanation. It frightens off someone like me.
The page opens with English index names and 'מדד' without explaining them. Older readers will think it's not for them and leave.
Dark background with grey text. The colour legend and small notes are hard to read even enlarged.
The cost bar uses colours that are close (orange, yellow, red, grey) and I couldn't tell them apart
The amounts are already filled in and there are sliders. It's not clear the result is just an example until you type your own.
Nothing says whether the money can go down; it only talks about costs
Too many numbers per row (two sums per bank plus notes), which makes me anxious
I couldn't tell who runs the site 'מקור'
